brief.subject: Diesel drops under $6 as truckload demand softens
brief.headline: Diesel Falls Below $6 While Truckload Volumes Slip and Rejections Ease
brief.dek: Diesel dropped 19.0 cents to $5.937, truckload volume weakened, and spot rates firmed to $3.56 as rejections hit their lowest since early May.
brief.lede: The U.S. average retail diesel price fell 19.0 cents to $5.937 per gallon. That relief arrives as truckload demand softens and carriers lose some pricing leverage.

sections.heading: Diesel Breaks Below $6
bullets: $5.937 per gallon: the national average retail diesel price for the week of 2026-11-16.
Down 19.0 cents (3.1%) from the prior week, a meaningful cut to per-mile fuel cost.
Down 33.9 cents over four weeks, so the decline is a trend, not a one-week blip.
Fuel surcharges are pegged to this benchmark, so expect surcharge payments to shrink as prices fall.

sections.heading: Truckload Demand Cools
bullets: 68: SONAR's Pricing Power Index fell as truckload demand weakened, trimming carriers' negotiating leverage.
13th percentile: accepted truckload volume gave back its recent gains, so expect fewer loads to choose from.
Tender rejections eased to their lowest level since early May, a sign capacity is loosening.
$3.56: the national spot rate still firmed, and broker RXO says the market is not turning deflationary.

sections.heading: Amazon Widens Fuel Surcharge
bullets: 3.5%: Amazon's fuel and logistics surcharge will extend to bulk storage and replenishment transportation fees.
The change takes effect in February, which shows shippers are still under pressure from fuel costs.

sections.heading: Ocean Rates High, Capacity Building
bullets: Ocean container spot rates are still 50% above a year ago, driven by congestion and fuel costs.
A growing vessel fleet and the return of Red Sea services could bring overcapacity, which would shift import timing for drayage.

sections.heading: Stolen-Vehicle Ring Busted
bullets: $4.5 million: police recovered 96 stolen vehicles that were headed to West Africa.
12 arrests so far and two suspects still wanted, a reminder to keep securing equipment at yards and stops.
